title: BPGS Blended Strategy Report (v3: DRN regime redefinition)
summary: Update from 2026-07-08: the DRN (Descent/Recovery/Normal) regime definition is redefined from a percent-drawdown ratio (T=12%, f=0.9) to a causal, fixed-anchor log-recovered-fraction formula (T=12%, f_lo=0.5, 2-day lag) -- the old formula divided by the current, shrinking drawdown and self-reinforced as price recovered, flipping its Descent-vs-Recovery separation sign after 2012; the new formula anchors to the trough once and holds up across both eras. Validated against real strategy-switching value (MR wins Descent+Recovery, MOM wins Normal, both in-sample and out-of-sample) rather than SPY-only separation. M4 (fixed vol-target) also has its Descent risk budget raised from 13% to 20% (matching Recovery), the best of four tested variants on out-of-sample Sharpe/Sortino. Same two-tab structure (HML/DRN), M1 Kelly and M4 fixed-vol methods, manual per-regime weight editor, log-scale equity curves, regime shading, reproducibility config embedded.
author: Arvind Rajan

title: RMT Factor Model — PC Structure & Portfolio Attribution

title: The Plausible-Worlds Engine — Simulating World States, Not Price Paths
summary: Essay II. An ideation report: replace Monte Carlo over asset prices with a generator of coherent world states — including states that have never occurred — governed by explicit plausibility rules, then infer asset prices within each world through structural channels. Survey of what exists, honest pitfalls, and a proposed architecture. Companion to Meta-Engine Design and Essay I, The Next-State Engine.
author: Arvind Rajan

title: The Next-State Engine — From Crisis Detection to State Anticipation
summary: Essay I. An ideation report: instead of fitting one predictive model to history, anticipate the probability-weighted next states of the world — macro, political, structural — and map each state to the predictive model that should govern it. Survey of what exists, honest pitfalls, and a proposed architecture built from the meta-engine's existing parts. Companion to Meta-Engine Design and Essay II, The Plausible-Worlds Engine.
author: Arvind Rajan

title: Sector Attribution Dashboard

MOM shows growing Technology concentration in OOS (AI/mega-cap momentum trade); MR's Financial Services allocation shows classic mean-reversion crisis alpha in 2008-2009.
